newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-CountryRoad sells part of US operation.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-CountryRoad sells part of US operation.

text.p: Australian clothing retailer Country Road Ltd said on Friday it had agreed to sell 25 percent of its U.S. operations to Japanese trading house Itochu Corp and that Itochu would market Country Road products in Japan.

Under the retailing and manufacturing agreement, Itochu would also provide global product sourcing, fashion market knowledge, manufacturing, distribution and logistics expertise to Country Road, the Australian retailer said.

"Under the terms of the agreement ITOCHU will buy 25 percent of Country Road's U.S. operations (and), in partnership with Itochu Fashion System Co Ltd, sub-license World Co Ltd to market Country Road products in Japan," Country Road said.
Itochu Fashion System, a wholly owned unit of Itochu, provides support services for fashion brands entering the Japanese market, Country Road said.

"Our agreement with Itochu provides a platform for Country Road to go forward internationally and achieve its vision of worldwide recognition for the brand," Country Road chief executive Mike Howell said in a statement.
"We will be able to utilise Itochu's existing relationships with leading raw material suppliers and influential apparel manufacturers and retailers around the world.
"This will be of enormous benefit to our U.S. operations and indeed to all our markets."
The agreement is to be signed at Country Road's annual meeting in November, the company said.

Country Road did not put a figure on Itochu's investment in its U.S. operations. Howell said he was confident Country Road now had the foundations for moving to a profitable operation in the United States.
In Japan, World Co Ltd plans to open Country Road flagship stores in prime sites in Tokyo and Osaka and a number of shops within department stores in japan, Country Road said.
"Country Road will join Itochu's stable of internationally acclaimed brands such as Giorgio Armani, Guess? Inc, Tommy Hilfiger, Katherine Hamnett and J. Crew," Country Road said.
"Both the Japanese expansion -- and the U.S. agreement -- provide further progress in Country Road's planned expansion and brand development internationally," it added.
